Vocabulary · 1 of 8

Return · how much your money grew

return = (exit − entry) ÷ entrywhat you got out, minus what you put in, as a share of what you put in

The engine does the same sum on the whole portfolio, after costs: (end ÷ start) − 1. ₹10,00,000 → ₹11,50,000 is +15%.

Worked example · Zomato, Session 1
  1. 1Entry price: bought at ₹58 a share (26 Apr 2023)
  2. 2Exit price: sold at ₹184 a share (27 May 2024)
  3. 3Subtract what you paid from what you got: 184 − 58 = ₹126 profit per share
  4. 4Divide by what you paid: 126 ÷ 58 = 2.17
  5. 5As a percentage: +217% (a ₹58 stake became ₹184)
Zomato daily closes, NSE via the Nubra SDK (data/csv/ZOMATO.csv): about ₹58 on 26 Apr 2023, ₹184 on 27 May 2024 (the Session 1 story).
Vocabulary · 2 of 8

CAGR · growth per year

CAGR = (end ÷ start) ^ (1 ÷ years) − 1the one steady yearly rate that would have produced the same end result

Zomato again

₹58 → ₹184 in 13 months = 3.17x. 3.17 ^ (1 ÷ 1.09) − 1 ≈ +190% a year. Nobody repeats that; it is one lucky year, annualised.

Worked example · ₹10,00,000 → ₹14,40,000 in 2 years
  1. 1End ÷ start: 14,40,000 ÷ 10,00,000 = 1.44 (the money grew 1.44x)
  2. 21 ÷ years = 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5, so take the square root: 1.44 ^ 0.5 = 1.20
  3. 3Minus 1: 1.20 − 1 = +20% a year
  4. 4Not 44 ÷ 2 = 22%. Year two grew on top of year one's gains. That is compounding.
  5. 5Check: 10,00,000 × 1.2 × 1.2 = 14,40,000 ✓
Zomato: 26 Apr 2023 to 27 May 2024 is 397 days ≈ 1.09 years; 184 ÷ 58 = 3.17. The engine uses bars instead of years: (1 + return) ^ (246 ÷ bars) − 1, so a 3-month test and a 12-month test compare.
Vocabulary · 3 of 8

Max drawdown · the worst fall

drawdown = (trough − peak) ÷ peakthe biggest such fall in the whole test is the max drawdown
Worked example · Paytm, Session 1
  1. 1Peak: the highest your money reached. Say you bought at the top: ₹785 (Aug 2022)
  2. 2Trough: the lowest point after it: ₹317 (8 May 2024)
  3. 3Subtract the peak from the trough: 317 − 785 = −₹468
  4. 4Divide by the peak: −468 ÷ 785 = −60% max drawdown
  5. 5To get back to ₹785 from ₹317 you need +148%. Could you have held through that?
Paytm daily closes, NSE via the Nubra SDK (data/csv/PAYTM.csv): ₹784.70 on 17 Aug 2022 (the Session 1 buy), lowest close ₹317.14 on 8 May 2024; it later recovered to ₹1,277 (15 Oct 2025).
Vocabulary · 4 of 8 · the one we judge on

Sharpe ratio

The Sharpe ratio measures the excess return of an investment per unit of its total risk (volatility).

Sharpe = (Rp − Rf) ÷ σpRp = return of the strategy · Rf = risk-free return (a government bond; 0 in our engine) · σp = standard deviation of the returns: the wobble
  1. 1Daily numbers, five days: +1.2%, −0.9%, +0.4%, −1.1%, +0.7%. Average Rp = 0.06% a day; wobble σp = 1.01% a day.
  2. 2Divide: (0.06 − 0) ÷ 1.01 = 0.059. That is a daily Sharpe.
  3. 3Make it yearly: returns add up over 246 trading days, but the wobble only grows with √246 = 15.7. So daily Sharpe × √246: 0.059 × 15.7 = Sharpe ≈ 0.93
  4. 4That is the only reason you see a √ in our scorecard: same formula, computed on daily returns, then annualised.

Below 0: losing · about 1: decent · above 2: suspicious · above 3: check for look-ahead

Named after William F. Sharpe (1966). Engine: mean(returns) ÷ std(returns) × √(bars per year), risk-free 0 (backtest.py, metrics). Intraday uses √(bars per year) instead of √246.
Vocabulary · 5 of 8

Trades and win rate

Number of trades

Too few and the result is luck. Minimum 10 to qualify today.

Win rate

Share of trades that made money. 35% can still be profitable if winners are big.

Exposure

How much of the time you were in the market. 20% exposure with +5% is different from 100% with +5%.

Vocabulary · 6 of 8

Costs eat strategies

  • Brokerage: a fee per order (₹20 in today's engine)
  • Slippage: you never get the price you saw (0.05% today)
  • 300 trades × both = a strategy that "worked" now loses

Rule

If a backtest ignores costs, it is a story, not a test.

Vocabulary · 7 of 8 · remember this one

In-sample vs out-of-sample

In-sample

The data you looked at while building the rule. You tuned it here, so of course it works here.

Out-of-sample

Data the rule has never seen. The only result that means anything.

Today's data stops at 30 June 2026. July to September is locked away. That is where you will be judged.

Vocabulary · 8 of 8

Timeframe · how big is one bar?

1d1h30m15m5m1m

Daily

246 bars a year. Slow, cheap, readable. The default today.

Intraday

Thousands of bars a year. More trades, more costs, more noise. Data from Sep 2025.

Your choice

One line in your file: TIMEFRAME = "15m". The engine loads the right data and annualises correctly.

Five ways the past fools you

Why most backtests lie

Look-ahead

Using information you would not have had yet.

Real exampleA rule that peeks one day ahead, on our 52 stocks: +316% in a year, 99% of trades win. Impossible in real life. Our engine blocks it.

Overfitting

Tuning a rule until it fits the past perfectly.

Real exampleWe tried 41 moving-average pairs on Jul-Dec 2025. Best one: Sharpe 2.01. Same rule on Jan-Jun 2026: Sharpe -1.87.

Survivorship

Testing only the winners that are still around.

Real exampleOur own data uses today's NIFTY 50. Stocks that fell out during the year are missing, so every result here is a little too rosy.

Costs ignored

Forgetting that every trade costs money.

Real exampleA student's 5-minute breakout: +3% before costs, -35% after. 21,707 trades, about ₹89 each.

Data snooping

Trying many ideas and showing only the lucky one.

Real example50 coin-flip strategies on our data: the luckiest made +15%, Sharpe 1.43. Pure chance. 12 of 50 beat our best real example.
Examples computed on the repo data (52 stocks, Jul 2025-Jun 2026) with the engine and engine-validation/VALIDATION.md; costs = brokerage Rs 20 or 0.03% + 0.03% slippage.

What your file must look like

One function. That's the whole contract.

TIMEFRAME = "1d"                      # or "1h", "15m", …

def strategy(df):
    # df: date, open, high, low, close, volume  (oldest first)
    fast = df["close"].rolling(20).mean()
    slow = df["close"].rolling(50).mean()
    return (fast > slow).astype(int)     # +1 long, 0 flat, −1 short, per row

In

one stock's candles

Out

a position for every row

Engine

runs it on all 52, equal weight, next-bar fills, costs, scorecard

Before you start: this is a tough challenge

Why most strategies lost this year

1 · The market went nowhere

+0.1%

Buy-and-hold of all 52 stocks for the whole year. Strategies that need a trend (crossovers, breakouts) had none to ride.

2 · Every trade costs money

₹89

What one round trip costs on a ₹1 lakh position (brokerage + slippage). The 5-minute breakout earned ₹7 per trade before costs.

3 · Chop rewards patience

0.31

The only winner bet on prices returning to normal (mean reversion), and traded rarely. That is the Sharpe to beat.

Fewer, better trades. Fit the idea to the market you have. Beat 0.31 and you have done something real.

Buy-and-hold, same universe, 1 Jul 2025 to 30 Jun 2026 (daily): +0.12%. ORB cost decomposition from engine-validation/VALIDATION.md (Rs 7.3 gross per trade vs Rs 89 cost per round trip).
The competition

Rules of the game

1 · 25 minutes

Submit any time; resubmit freely, your latest entry counts. Showdown closes submissions itself at 00:00: nothing is accepted after.

2 · Submit in Showdown

Same link as the quizzes. Paste your whole .py file and the SUBMIT line it printed.

3 · We run your file

Your file is re-run automatically on July to September 2026, data nobody has seen. That result is your score, not the number you paste.

4 · Judged on Sharpe

Highest hidden Sharpe wins. At least 10 trades. Tie: the earlier submission wins.

5 · Not eligible if

your SUBMIT line doesn't match your file, it peeks at the future, it crashes, or it imports anything beyond pandas and numpy.

6 · Reward

The student who cracks the best strategy gets a reward.

Judge: safety check of the code, re-run on public data (must match your SUBMIT line), then the hidden-data run. Showdown "Strategy Showdown" round opens with the clock.

A path, not a promise

1 · Maths

Statistics and probability, properly. Linear algebra. That is the real moat.

2 · Code

Python and pandas fluently. Then one systems language. Git from day one.

3 · Build in public

Backtests, tools, contributions. A GitHub profile beats a CV line.

4 · Markets

Read, paper trade, keep a journal. Microstructure before prediction.

Roles exist for builders, data engineers, researchers and traders. You do not have to trade to work here.
